agent noun

classical

Liv. 22.33.1: speculātor Carthāginiēnsis
Caes. BG 2.11 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. spy: (tēctus) speculātor

speculātor, speculātōris m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a spy, a scout

Other words

  • explōrātor, explōrātōris m. — a scout; a spy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.12.2 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Not in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • ēmissārius, ēmissāriī m. — an agent sent out, an emissary, a spy

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.2.3 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • per eōsdem diēs speculātor Carthāginiēnsis, quī per biennium fefellerat, Rōmae dēprēnsus praecīsīsque manibus dīmissus

    about the same time a Carthaginian spy, who had gone undetected for two years, was caught at Rome and let go with his hands cut offLiv. 22.33.1

See also agent, army, war, police.
